title: Vendor onboarding: weighted risk paths + insurance-subsidy experiment
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Reduce procurement friction for engineering teams while maintaining risk controls by introducing weighted risk-tier onboarding flows and an insurance-subsidy path for high-risk vendors.

Problem: Enterprise procurement teams currently block or slow integration of certain vendors because manual review of security questionnaires and insurance verification is time-consuming. This increases time-to-contract and causes feature delays for product teams.

Hypothesis: Exposing a risk-weighted onboarding path plus an optional insurance-subsidy option (where vendors can present qualifying insurance for an automated credit to reduce procurement friction) will reduce manual review time by >=40%, increase vendor completion rate by >=15%, and maintain acceptable risk (no increase in post-onboard incidents).

Scope (in):
- Design and implement conditional questionnaire flows in the vendor portal keyed to a weighted risk score.
- Build an 'insurance-subsidy' verification microflow that validates basic policy metadata (carrier, policy number, coverage level) and issues a standardized credit token for procurement.
- Instrument metrics and dashboards (time-to-complete, manual-review volume, conversion rate).
- Legal / insurance copy review and standardized contract clause templates.

Out of scope:
- Full SOC2 attestation automation (we will link to existing SOC2 packages and evidence upload, not replace the attestation process).
- Integrations to legacy SSO directories beyond the minimal OAuth connector for vendor portal auth.

Experiment design:
- Control: existing onboarding flow (full questionnaire, manual reviewer assignment).
- Variant A: Weighted risk-path where low-risk answers auto-fasttrack; medium/high risk go to targeted reviewer with recommended mitigation checklist.
- Variant B: Same as Variant A + optional insurance-subsidy flow: qualifying vendors can submit insurance metadata and receive a procurement credit token that reduces manual scrutiny.
- Randomized rollout across new vendor signups for 6 weeks or until statistically significant differences are observed.

Success metrics (primary):
- Reduction in median time from vendor initiation to procurement approval (target >= 40% reduction).
- Decrease in manual reviewer assignments per vendor (target >= 35% reduction).

Secondary metrics:
- Vendor completion rate of onboarding (target +15%).
- Number of vendors using insurance-subsidy and their downstream contract conversion rate.
- No material increase in security incidents attributable to onboarded vendors.

Data flows & compliance notes:
- Insurance verification will only store hashed policy metadata and reference tokens; raw policy documents will be stored in a customer-managed S3 with KMS encryption if required.
- SOC2 evidence links will remain opt-in; we will not parse or store PII beyond verification needs.
- Security & Legal will sign off on the exact risk thresholds and permitted automations.

Rollout plan:
1) Week 1-2: Product + design finalize flows and acceptance criteria. 2) Week 3-4: Engineering builds portal conditional logic, insurance microflow, and metrics instrumentation. 3) Week 5: Internal pilot with procurement team + 10 vendors. 4) Week 6-8: A/B rollout to 25% of new vendor signups, expand to 100% if targets are met.

Dependencies:
- IAM team to enable vendor portal OAuth connector (ENG-46721).
- Billing team to accept and redeem procurement credit tokens (ENG-48901).
- Legal sign-off on insurance clause templates (PM-9113 referenced).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Vendors may falsify insurance metadata. Mitigation: We will perform carrier lookups for all insurance-subsidy claims and mark tokens as provisional until carrier confirmation.
- Risk: Automated fast-track misses nuanced control gaps. Mitigation: Keep a sampling of fast-tracked vendors for manual audit and tune weights weekly.

Next steps:
- Kickoff meeting scheduled 2026-03-16 with all stakeholders.
- Design review + prototype due 2026-03-24.
- Security deep-dive and threat model required before engineering begins (security_review_required flag set).
